Team Breakdown
Game Breakdown

Bandits Run Wild in Capital City

The HC Calgary Bandits turned a road trip into a demolition derby Saturday, steamrolling the Capital City Knights 8-1 behind a hat trick from Wyatt Hamilton and a four-point night from Ryder O'Reilly. What was supposed to be a competitive affair was effectively decided before the first intermission, as the Bandits scored four unanswered goals in a span of just over three minutes to bury the home side early.

Hamilton opened the scoring with 4:42 left in the first period, finishing a feed from Huxley Copeland and Manakveer Grewal. Just 19 seconds later, O'Reilly struck for what would stand as the game-winner, and when Kobe Voyer made it 3-0 off a Beau Pestun setup, the Knights were reeling. Hamilton added his second of the period with 1:23 remaining, and the rout was on. The Bandits kept their foot on the gas in the middle frame, with Hamilton completing his hat trick at the 5:22 mark and Grewal adding another to make it 6-0 before the Knights had even found their legs. Capital City finally broke through in the third when Kaden O'Connell potted a power-play goal off assists from Kashton Fedun and Luka Thiessen, but any thoughts of a comeback were quickly extinguished as Voyer and Grewal answered right back to restore the six-goal cushion.

The story of the night was the goaltending disparity. Capital City's Blake Brassard was under siege from the opening puck drop, facing 45 shots and surrendering eight goals in a performance he'll want to forget. At the other end, Baron Wilson came on in relief and turned aside all 22 shots he faced in 20 minutes of work, slamming the door shut on any faint Knights momentum. The Bandits' balanced attack, combined with a defensive effort that limited Capital City to zero first-period shots, made this one a laugher from start to finish. If there's a silver lining for the Knights, it's that they managed 17 shots over the final two periods, but against a team firing on all cylinders like Calgary, moral victories were all that remained.
